vignette: A 22-year-old man is quadriplegic after a diving injury at C5. On the third day a nurse finds him flushed and sweating above the neck with a headache and a blood pressure of 220/120 and a pulse of 48. His bladder is distended.
explanation: A noxious stimulus below a lesion above T6 triggers massive sympathetic discharge from the disconnected splanchnic outflow, producing hypertension with reflex bradycardia and flushing above the lesion: autonomic dysreflexia. Emptying the bladder is the treatment.
